title: Prefetch Concurrency Diagnostic Log
summary: Working log of experiments exploring how prefetch windows and concurrent streams interact with fused attention kernels. Goal: find heuristics that reduce tail latency without sacrificing steady-state throughput when mixing short and long sequences.
experimental_setup: Cluster: 4x A100-80GB (single worker used for microbench). CUDA: 12.1, cuDNN: 8.9. Runtime branch: feature/prefetch-adapt-v2 (PR 987). Flash kernel: flash-attn v2 patched with paged-kv hooks. Triton: 2.2. Batcher: continuous-batcher with soft-slice=32ms. Workload: synthetic mixture — 60% short (seq=64), 30% med (seq=512), 10% long (seq=2048). Concurrency sweep: {1,4,8,16,32} concurrent requests. Prefetch window swept: {0,16,64,256} tokens. Fusion enabled/disabled. Measurements: p50/p90/p99 token-latency, GPU SM utilization, achieved TFLOPS, kernel occupancy, L2_bw, and PCIe transfer times for paged path.
profiling_steps: 1) Run single-kernel microbench (no batcher) for each seq to establish baseline kernel latency. 2) Re-run with continuous-batcher and prefetch windows to measure queueing. 3) Capture per-kernel CUPTI traces and nvprof summaries for runs with and without fusion. 4) Use perf counters (register spills, l1 hit/miss) to detect register pressure. 5) Reproduce high tail-latency with randomized inter-arrival times. 6) Swap to unfused kernels to compare overhead from launches vs register pressure.
key_findings:
- Small-sequence (seq<=64) paths see worse p99 when fused ops are always enabled. Hypothesis: fusion increases register usage, dropping occupancy and hurting small workloads where memory is not the bottleneck.
- Prefetch window >64 tokens reduces p99 for long sequences (seq>=1024) by ~18% due to reduced flash-paged page faults and fewer host-device syncs.
- High concurrency mixes (>=16) show KV cache contention: memory allocator fragmentation + pinned memory exhaustion causing spikes in allocation latency.
- Using 2 CUDA streams per request (compute + I/O) reduced latency variance by ~12% at concurrency 8 but increased CPU-side context switches; net CPU usage rose ~20%.
- Fused kernels provided 15-22% lower steady-state per-token TFLOPS for long batches but regress on mixed short/long workloads due to lower parallelism for small tiles.
microbench_results:
(representative, single-worker A100)
- Single request, seq=2048, batch=1, fused on: p50=9.6ms/token, p99=12.1ms/token, achieved 42 TFLOPS.
- Single request, seq=64, batch=1, fused on: p50=1.1ms/token, p99=2.9ms/token, occupancy=38%.
- Mixed workload concurrency=16, prefetch=64, fused on: p50=1.9ms/token, p99=8.3ms/token, observed intermittent 40-90ms allocation stalls.
- Same mix, fused off: p50=2.2ms/token, p99=6.7ms/token — higher median but better tail for short seqs.
Notes: absolute numbers are noisy; re-run with 30 minute steady-state window recommended.
anomalies_and_hypotheses:
- Observed weird periodic p99 spikes every ~120s correlated with a background GC-like behavior in pinned-buffer recycler. Hypothesis: recycler does a compaction sweep triggered by peak allocations and blocks callers.
- When fusion threshold lowered to only long-seq paths, p99 improved for mixed traffic. Suspect a sweet spot cutoff based on effective tile count > 8.
- Prefetch combined with fusion sometimes causes double-buffer copy contention on host pinned memory; potential bug in our paged-attention page-evict logic leading to synchronous copies.
next_steps: 1) Add metrics: pinned_alloc_count, recycler_pause_ms to runtime telemetry. 2) Run ablation to find fusion cutoff: vary seq-bucket thresholds and measure p99 for mixed loads. 3) Instrument register spill counters and L2 read/write per-kernel to confirm register pressure hypothesis. 4) Implement lightweight per-request stream affinity (bind compute to a fixed pair of streams) and remeasure CPU overhead. 5) Prepare PR with adaptive fusion policy (disable fusion below tile-threshold) and A/B test in staging for 48h.
raw_commands:
# example harness commands run locally
./bench_runner --model=gpt-like --kernel=flash --seq=2048 --batch=1 --triton-workers=4 --repeat=200
./bench_runner --mix=short:60,med:30,long:10 --concurrency=16 --prefetch=64 --fusion=on --trace=cupti:out.cupti
sudo perf record -e r6000 -a -- ./bench_runner ...
# toggle fusion flag
export RW_FUSION_ENABLED=0 && ./serve_inference_loadtest ...
notes_to_self:
- Don't assume fused==faster for all workloads. Add a small regression test that runs a mixed-short-long trace on every runtime PR that touches kernel fusion.
- Talk to Chen about allocator knobs; he suspects the pinned allocator threshold is too low for mixed traffic which causes frequent pin/unpin.
- Diego to run longer 24h steady-state run on dedicated 8-GPU rig to surface rare recycler pauses.
- Keep an eye on the memory footprint when enabling 2 streams per request; might blow out OOM for dense KV caches.
- Draft the adaptive-fusion PR description with these microbench bullets and link to perf outputs in the PR.
